summary: The fixture now uses `ps -ww` when observing the queued gate marker, preventing truncation of the inline gate program and its trailing `gpg-dsh-install-wait` marker. The existing installation-drain test also sets an 80-column environment so the long gate argv would reproduce the clipping regression. No introduced defects were found.

evidence: tests/fixtures/gpg-dsh-migration.sh line 145 now uses `ps -ww -p ... -o args=`, so the full argv including `gpg-dsh-install-wait` survives display-width clipping.
tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts lines 815-816 set `COLUMNS=80` for the installation-drain regression test, exercising the clipped-argument scenario.
The base commit used `ps -p ...` without `-ww` at the same gate observation, so the candidate directly implements the requested widening.
